To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
carcass and meat quality characteristics of pigs selected for RFI are influenced by diet.
carcasses from pigs selected for low feed efficiency were leaner than carcasses from pigs that were more efficient.
pigs selected for low RFI had leaner carcasses, and chops from pigs selected for low residual feed intake were juicer than chops from high RFI pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of divergent selection for feed intake and the effects of feeding low- or high-energy diets on carcass characteristics, pork quality, and sensory characteristics.
the impact of divergent selection for RFI, and feeding LEHF or HELF diets, on meat quality and carcasses composition of pigs.
the impact of diet on the quality of pork from pigs selected for residual feed efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
carcasses from LRFI were leaner than carcasses from HRFI, and pigs fed LEHF had greater loin depth and lighter HCW than pigs fed HELD.
the divergent RFI lines were different in carcass composition.
the energy content of the diets had a greater influence on carcass composition than the divergent selection for RFI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pigs with low residual feed intake are leaner, have greater percent lean, and less fat depth than high residual feed intake pigs.
carcasses and pork quality are influenced by selection for RFI, but not by diet energy content.
the divergent RFI selection lines have a greater impact on pork quality traits than the diet fed to the pigs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy content of the diets fed to pigs impacts carcass composition and quality.
pigs with low RFI have leaner carcasses and pork with greater sensory juiciness than pigs with high RFI.
pigs divergently selection for RFI have differences in carcass and meat quality that are not influenced by diet energy content.
